What Pipeline welcomes audiences to our newly renovated gallery space in Eastern Market, featuring two solo exhibitions: Demario Dotson _Error Fo' O' Fo'_ and Bailey Scieszka _Every Force Evolves a Form_. 

Opening reception Friday, November 13, 6 - 9 PM

Demario Dotson 
_Error Fo' O' Fo'_ 
November 13, 2026 - January 16, 2027

[Press Release](https://whatpipeline.com/exhibitions/73demariodotson/Demario_Dotson_Error_Fo_O_Fo_Press_Release.pdf)

Demario Dotson _Error Fo' O' Fo'_ is a pioneering multimedia installation existing at the intersection of Black feminism, queer activism, and Black superhero narratives.

Dotson is an Atlanta native and multidisciplinary artist working across 3D animation, digital media, music composition, textiles, and installation. Dotson received an MFA from Cranbrook Academy of Art in 2021, where he was awarded a Director’s Fellowship. Dotson’s residencies include Queer.Archive.Work and ACRE. Dotson has exhibited at Cranbrook Art Museum, What Pipeline, Ann Arbor Art Center, Mana Contemporary and Atlanta Art Fair. Dotson was highlighted by Bemis Center for Contemporary Arts as an emerging Black artist to watch and contributed animation to Tiff Massey’s _Get Big 1.0_ as part of the 2021 DLECTRICITY festival and Salt City Techno Poem at the Apollo Theater. Dotson was named a 2022 Kresge Artist Fellow in Film & Music and, most recently, a 2024 Knight New Work recipient.

Bailey Scieszka 
_Every Force Evolves a Form_ 
November 13, 2026 - January 16, 2027

[Press Release](https://whatpipeline.com/exhibitions/74baileyscieszka/Bailey_Scieszka_Every_Force_Evolves_a_Form_Press_Release.pdf)

Bailey Scieszka _Every Force Evolves a Form_ explores couture sexuality, reality tv and contemporary American politics through clowning, handmade paper and Scieszka’s use of signature iconography.

Scieszka is an intermedia artist from Detroit working across drawing, painting, puppet dramas, installation, papermaking, and video. Through a rotating cast of personas animated by folly, he reimagines American history as an absurd pageant of conspiracy and myth. He received his BFA from Cooper Union, where he was awarded the Benjamin Menschel Grant, and his MFA in Art Practice from Stanford University.

Scieszka’s work has been exhibited at the Anderson Collection at Stanford University, Atlanta Contemporary, MOCAD (Detroit), White Columns (New York), What Pipeline (Detroit), and Maria Bernheim (Zürich and London). His puppet dramas have been presented at Paris Internationale, EMPAC, and NADA New York. His work has been featured in _The New Yorker_, _Vogue_, _The New York Times_, _Mousse_, _CURA_, _The Whitney Review_, and _Cultured_.

metadata.title: Home | Red Arrow Gallery
metadata.description: Red Arrow was founded in 2006 in Joshua Tree, California, and relocated to Nashville, Tennessee, in 2014. Beginning with bold roots in the desert, the gallery has since become a cornerstone of Nashville’s contemporary art scene. Helmed by Gallerist Katie Shaw and Director Ashley Layendecker, Red Arrow Gallery has always been women-led. Red Arrow champions artists with local/international ties whose work feels fresh, uncompromising, and inspired. The gallery connects southern-based artists with the global contemporary art conversation while introducing outside perspectives to Nashville, further establishing the city as a growing hub for arts and culture. With a program rooted in collaboration, care, and rigor, Red Arrow is committed to building artists' careers, fostering relationships, and putting Nashville and its artists on the international map.

**Tanya Weddemire Gallery** is a Brooklyn-based contemporary art gallery, established in **2022** and located in **Industry City, Brooklyn**. Founded by Tanya Weddemire, the gallery is dedicated to presenting the work of emerging and established artists whose practices explore identity, heritage, and contemporary narratives. Through thoughtful curatorial programming and strong community engagement, the gallery presents exhibitions, artist projects, and collaborations that connect cultural and historical perspectives with current artistic practices. Its programming is also supported by philanthropic initiatives that reinforce the gallery’s commitment to cultural access and impact. Exhibitions highlight a range of mediums including painting, sculpture, and mixed media allowing artists to communicate layered stories and lived experiences through material and form. Tanya Weddemire Gallery has presented artists through both in-gallery exhibitions and international art fairs, including **The Armory Show,  EXPO Chicago, 1-54 Contemporary African Art Fair,** IN**SCOPE Art Show, Atlanta Art Fair and the Affordable Art Fair**. Anchored in the philosophy of **community, culture, and legacy**, the gallery remains committed to building meaningful connections between artists, collectors, and global audiences.
